title: Architectural Shifts
desc: The structural changes under the hood in 2.0.
lede: The big 2.0 changes are structural. Here's what moved and why each shift matters.
body:
At a glance
  • One-shot subprocess → managed TTS Server.
  • Worker loop → orchestrator.
  • Engine-ID branches → plugin manifests.
  • Raw-file checks → validated artifacts.

From one-shot subprocess to a managed TTS Server

Synthesis runs in a long-lived, supervised process with a watchdog, instead of being spun up ad hoc. Engines can crash and restart without losing app state.

From a worker loop to an orchestrator

Scheduling, progress, and recovery are centralized. The orchestrator owns the queue and reconciliation rather than a single loop doing everything.

From engine-ID branches to plugin manifests

Behavior is declared, not hard-coded. What an engine supports comes from its manifest, so adding an engine doesn't mean adding special cases across the app.

From raw-file checks to validated artifacts

Completion is judged by validated artifact metadata. A file existing is no longer mistaken for finished work. See Artifacts, Reuse & Recovery.
